evidence_detail: Indian STU buses run at much higher load factors. The India value is CO2 only and not valid for BRTS or intercity.
recommendation: Label the unit as passenger-km. Use the India STU factor for Indian intracity buses, with a caveat. Intercity needs a separate sourced factor (none found yet).

evidence_detail: UK rail factors track the UK grid (0.131 kg/kWh in 2026). India's grid (~0.71) is ~5x more carbon-intensive, so UK metro factors are not transferable. No primary Indian per-pkm metro factor found. A TERI-input estimate of ~0.03 is derived, not published.
recommendation: Do not ship a UK value for Indian metros. Source per-system values (DMRC/BMRCL sustainability reports or CDM PDDs), or derive transparently from traction kWh, pkm and the CEA factor as a documented calculation with its own record.

evidence_value: 0.22928 with RF / 0.13552 without RF (GB domestic avg, 2026); 0.14253 / 0.0842 intl non-UK avg
evidence_detail: Radiative forcing basis not stated. The unit should be passenger-km. DESNZ 'International, to/from non-UK' is the closest DESNZ category for flights inside India.
recommendation: Store with-RF and without-RF as separate factors and show which one is used. Pick the DESNZ non-UK category (or a reviewed Indian aviation source) for Indian domestic flights.

evidence_detail: Zero operational emissions is correct by definition. Life-cycle (manufacture, food energy) is excluded.
recommendation: Keep. Record system_boundary = operational only.

evidence_detail: 5.0 kg implies ~50 g of beef. climate-knowledge.ts says a 200 g serving = 12 kg (60 kg/kg). Neither serving is defined anywhere.
recommendation: Replace with recipe = ingredient grams x verified per-kg factors (deterministic tool). Publish the serving assumption. Note Indian diets rarely include beef. Prioritise dal, rice, paneer, chicken and egg recipes.

evidence_detail: Implies ~120 g chicken plus nothing else. Undocumented.

evidence_detail: Boundary undefined: is it the meal, or only delivery transport and packaging? The cook-home action (3.2 kg/week for 3 dinners) implies ~1.07 kg per delivery, contradicting 0.6. Logging 'chicken meal' + 'food delivery' may double count the meal.

recommendation: Rule: appliance entries are an attribution view of household kWh, never additive when a bill or meter reading covers the same period. Enforce in CarbonCalculationService and the dashboard.

recommendation: Retire both until a sourced, garment-type-specific factor set (kg CO2e per garment type or per kg fibre) is reviewed. Show 'not estimated' rather than a guess.

evidence_detail: 'Generic device' is undefined: phone, laptop and TV differ by an order of magnitude. Manufacturer product environmental reports exist per model, not per 'item'.
recommendation: Product-type-specific factors from manufacturer LCAs (per model, with year), or spend-based EEIO with an Indian or global table. Never one generic number.

evidence_detail: Boundary undefined (parcel delivery only, or product included?). Overlaps clothing and electronics.
recommendation: Model as a delivery leg only (sourced last-mile factor). The product is logged separately.

evidence_detail: 'item' undefined. Double counts with meals cooked from those groceries.
recommendation: Choose one food accounting path (purchases OR meals) per user and period. Never both.

evidence_detail: Unit undefined (bag? kg?). Waste emissions depend on the treatment route (landfill, open burning, composting). DESNZ waste factors are UK-specific. food_waste overlaps the food already counted at purchase or meal; plastic_bottle overlaps the purchase.
recommendation: Hold until an India-relevant waste source (e.g. IPCC 2006 Vol.5 methods with Indian parameters) is reviewed. Count disposal only, never the embodied product again.

recommendation: See D13.

evidence_detail: No derivation. The 45% figure is US-household context.
recommendation: Remove. Compute from user kWh if needed.

item: 2500 kg/yr labelled as 6.8-8.5 kg/day; daily budget 8.5
evidence_detail: 2500/365 = 6.85, so 8.5 kg/day = 3103 kg/yr (+24%). The target is IGES et al. 2019, not IPCC (IPCC sets no per-person budget). It covers the full consumption footprint (housing, goods, services, leisure), not only the 5 categories the app tracks, so comparing tracked emissions with it overstates progress.
recommendation: Cite IGES 2019. Show 6.85 kg/day only alongside a clear 'whole-lifestyle target vs partial tracking' caveat. Do not claim 'aligned with Paris'.

recommendation: Report 'logged emissions' and 'estimated reductions from specific adopted actions' separately. Compute a reduction only against the user's own measured history with enough coverage, and label it an estimate.
